Lemma
[Zeros of a vector field] ↗ thm:brouwer-fixed-point-theorem 1. ch9:9.1-lem-1\group Nonlinear Elliptic PDE

Assume the continuous function $\mathbf{v} : \R ^n \to \R ^n$ satisfies \[ \mathbf{v}(x) \cdot x \geq 0 \quad \text{if } |x| = r, \tag {8} \] for some $r > 0$. Then there exists a point $x \in B(0,r)$ such that \[ \mathbf{v}(x) = 0. \]

Proof

\sketch If $\mathbf v$ had no zero in $B(0,r)$, the map $\mathbf w(x)=-r\mathbf v(x)/|\mathbf v(x)|$ would map the ball continuously to its boundary. Brouwer gives a fixed point $z$, but then $|z|=r$ and $r^2=\mathbf w(z)\cdot z\leq 0$, a contradiction.

□
